fish.name: Confetti Fry
fish.flavor: Hatches by the thousand whenever the reef has something to celebrate. The reef always has something to celebrate.

fish.name: Penny Wrasse
fish.flavor: Shiny as a freshly minted coin and worth slightly less. Wishing wells have a strict policy about accepting them.

fish.name: Blushing Blenny
fish.flavor: Turns scarlet the instant it is observed. Marine biologists have been forced to study it entirely through gossip.

fish.name: Peppermint Dartfish
fish.flavor: Striped like a candy cane and quick as a sneeze. Smells faintly of December, even here in the warm shallows.

fish.name: Gossip Guppy
fish.flavor: Swims mouth-first into other fishes' business. Everything it knows about you, it learned from a snail.

fish.name: Sugarspun Damsel
fish.flavor: Its fins look spun from pink sugar and dissolve very slightly in warm water. It is enormously vain about this.

fish.name: Tidepool Tumbler
fish.flavor: Rolls end over end with every surge, apparently on purpose. Applause only encourages it.

fish.name: Parasol Tang
fish.flavor: Unfolds its dorsal fin at noon like a tiny beach umbrella, then charges passing fish rent for the shade.

fish.name: Lullaby Cardinal
fish.flavor: Hums a three-note song at dusk that makes the anemones close up cozy for the night. Hum it back and it will follow you home.

fish.name: Curio Cowfish
fish.flavor: Collects small shiny objects it cannot carry, then guards them anyway. Its hoard currently consists of one bottlecap.

fish.name: Ribbonwisp
fish.flavor: A ribbon that slipped off a present long ago and decided to make something of itself. It still curls when complimented.

fish.name: Mumbling Grunt
fish.flavor: Grunts constantly under its breath. Nobody has ever caught what it says, but you strongly suspect it is about you.

fish.name: Sundial Goby
fish.flavor: Basks on the same coral shelf all day, turning slowly to face the sun. The reef sets its naps by it.

fish.name: Marzipan Mimic
fish.flavor: Shaped suspiciously like whatever fish you were hoping to catch. Tastes of almonds and mild disappointment.

fish.name: Teaspoon Seapony
fish.flavor: Exactly one teaspoon of seahorse. Stirs itself into tidepools and refuses to dissolve, no matter how long you wait.

fish.name: Old Rope Eel
fish.flavor: Indistinguishable from a length of frayed dockline until it winks. Sailors who tie knots in one are owed exactly one favor.

fish.name: Widdershins Wrasse
fish.flavor: Swims exclusively anticlockwise, even when this is a terrible idea. Reef folk say catching one un-jinxes a bad week.

fish.name: Borrowed Blue
fish.flavor: Its colour is on loan from the sky, due back at sunset. At dusk it goes politely grey and waits for morning.

fish.name: Kettlewhistle Pipefish
fish.flavor: Whistles when the water reaches exactly the right temperature for tea. Reef hermits keep one instead of a clock.

fish.name: Fibbing Puffer
fish.flavor: Inflates to twice the size of its actual accomplishments. Deflates immediately when asked a follow-up question.

fish.name: Pocketwatch Snapper
fish.flavor: Ticks, audibly, at sixty beats to the minute. Nobody has ever found the watch, and at this point everyone is afraid to ask.

fish.name: Chandelier Drifter
fish.flavor: Drifts through the night reef trailing lit crystal arms, as if some grand ballroom sank politely out of sight. Do not waltz with it.

fish.name: Moth-Eaten Angel
fish.flavor: Full of small holes that let the sunlight through in lace patterns. Absolutely will not discuss where it has been hanging.

fish.name: Postcard Flounder
fish.flavor: Its back is a faded picture of somewhere lovely. Wish you were here, it implies, smugly.

fish.name: Velvet Purrfish
fish.flavor: Purrs when stroked along the dorsal fin. Scientists insist fish cannot purr; the fish purrs louder.

fish.name: Janus Butterflyfish
fish.flavor: Wears a false face at each end and, some say, a true one in the middle. It approaches and departs simultaneously.

fish.name: Widow's Lantern
fish.flavor: Carries a small green light said to be a lighthouse keeper's last candle. It has never once let it go out, and neither should you.

fish.name: Stitchwork Wanderer
fish.flavor: Sewn together from six kinds of fish by somebody with more thread than sense. It holds together beautifully and forgives easily.

fish.name: Porcelain Pilgrim
fish.flavor: Glazed blue-and-white like grandmother's good china, travelling the reef one coral shrine at a time. Handle it with the reverence you would show the good plates.

fish.name: Echo Parrot
fish.flavor: It is the reef's colours repeated back, slightly wrong. Catch one and somewhere a real parrotfish feels briefly plagiarised.

fish.name: Weathervane Wrasse
fish.flavor: Its stripes rearrange themselves a full day ahead of the weather. Three bands means bring a coat; nobody knows what four means, and it has been four all week.

fish.name: Vicar Moray
fish.flavor: Solemn, collared in white, and given to long, meaningful silences. The small fish of the parish confess to it anyway.

fish.name: Milkmoon Ray
fish.flavor: On full-moon nights it glides just under the surface like spilt moonlight that learned to swim. Touch nothing. Wish quietly.

fish.name: The Anemone Bride
fish.flavor: Wed to the reef in a ceremony nobody remembers attending. Her veil stings, her devotion is total, and the anemones bloom wherever she chooses to wait.

fish.name: Grandmother Pearl
fish.flavor: Old enough to remember this reef as bare rock, and patient enough to have watched every coral arrive. Ask nicely and she may tell you which ones were late.

fish.name: Choirbone
fish.flavor: Its skeleton is a set of hollow pipes, and the tide plays it in eight parts. On windless nights the whole cove goes quiet to listen.

fish.name: The Undertow's Favourite
fish.flavor: The undertow keeps it the way you might keep a lucky coin. When it circles, even the current holds its breath.

fish.name: Saint Elsewhere
fish.flavor: Revered in every tidepool it has never visited; shrines to it face away from the water, just in case. Catching it is a paradox the reef has agreed to overlook, once, for you.

fish.name: The Coral Cathedral
fish.flavor: A fish so old the reef built itself upon its back, spire by spire, parish by parish. When it rises, services are cancelled and the whole sea holds its hymn.

fish.name: The Last Colour
fish.flavor: The ocean once invented a colour and showed it to no one, and this small fish has worn it ever since. You will spend the rest of your life failing to describe it, and you will not mind.
